summary: 50-ft metal tower in Archuleta County, CO; the register dates it to 1970. Tribe-owned with no public access; a Colorado list marks it removed.

facts.design: 50-foot metal tower with a 7x7 ft cab inside a 4 ft catwalk; stair and landing design differs from common fire tower models
facts.status_note: A Colorado lookout list marks this tower removed; the register entry (registered 2010) does not confirm its current condition.

access.note: Owned and managed by the Southern Ute Indian Tribe; the register says there is no public access.

visit.trail_note: No public access, according to the register. Do not climb or enter without the tribe's permission.

events.note: Build year given by the register; no builder or design history found

evidence.supports: 50-foot metal tower that may be one of a kind
evidence.quote: The Sandoval Mesa Lookout is a 50' metal tower that may be one of a kind.

evidence.quote: It differs from the majorfire tower models in stair and landing design.

corrections.why: The register and the Colorado lookout list both place the site near 37.104 N, 107.324 W. The record's point is about 2 km to the east.
The Colorado lookout list marks Sandoval Mesa as Removed. The register text (2010) does not confirm current condition, so a person should check before this is applied.

notes_for_editor: Build year and design rest on the register alone (one source, 2010). The status conflict is real: the register describes the tower in the present tense, while the Colorado list (undated row) says Removed. No newer source was found; the Southern Ute Indian Tribe is the authority on current condition. Two searches gave no staffing, fire or build history, so none is in the story. The 50 ft figure is the register's stated tower height; a separate cab-floor height was not stated. The record's point is about 2 km east of both register coordinates; the location and status corrections are proposed, not applied. Tribal land with no public access: the story does not encourage visits.
